title: fill-real: an execution-grounded dataset for evaluating Solana trading strategies
description:
Almost every publicly shared backtest of Solana token strategies is computed on screen price: the value an aggregator reports on a polling interval. The price at which an order actually executes is different, and the difference is not symmetric noise that averages out — it is a directional bias large enough to invert conclusions.

Version 2.0 contains 1,746,551 rows across 7 files (25× the v1 release), collected from a live system on Solana mainnet between June and August 2026, including post-migration positions measured with real Jupiter fills, order-by-order execution telemetry, and 1.6M post-migration price trajectory points across 40,427 mints.

The screen-price bias, measured three independent ways:

  • Migration-speed strategy: screen price said +36%, real fills said −69% (n≈24k / 21k)
  • Entry gate cross-check: simulated −42.8%, real −1.1%
  • Exit policy calibration: simulated −29.8%, real −10.9%

The bias runs in both directions, which is what makes it dangerous. Screen price made a ruinous entry rule look profitable, and separately made reactive exit policies look far worse than they are. Screen price penalizes reactive policies and rewards illusory ones.

NEW IN v2 — an exhaustive condition sweep returns zero positives. Over 36,736 real-fill positions, every combination of 10 ex-ante features × 7 percentile cuts × 2 directions, plus 4 social booleans and one cross-strategy condition — 114 distinct conditions with n≥100 each — produced 0 with a positive mean. A sweep returning zero positives requires no multiple-comparison correction, because there is nothing to discount. Two sub-results: (a) win rate and median are actively misleading — three conditions win over half their trades and all lose money, with liqUsd≥204,183 winning 67.1% at a +12.53% median and a −7.33% mean; (b) ruin is predictable but profit is not — preBuyers≥326 cuts total-loss rate from 24.5% to 1.9% with a mean still at −3.25%. The predictable set and the profitable set are disjoint.

NEW IN v2 — the horizon-truncation bias is now bounded. v1 warned that series truncate near 36 minutes and called the resulting optimism unbounded. On 1,728 tokens with a full 190-minute horizon, the same tokens lose a further 31.7 percentage points of trimmed-mean multiple between minute 36 and minute 190 (0.9143 → 0.5970); 66.3% keep falling past the cutoff. This is a paired within-token estimate, so the drift is not a composition artifact — but that subsample's window (16–21 Aug) is a worse regime than the full population by −19.5 pp at the shared 36-minute mark, so the magnitude is a point estimate from one six-day window rather than a universal constant.

Further results: pool liquidity does not lead price (median lead 0 seconds across 150 collapses; at thresholds ≥15%, zero cases had any warning; median single-interval gap 97.2 pp). Real round-trip friction is 10.7% (7.79% entry overhead n=164, 2.91% exit slippage n=922) against a median best-window move of +8.3%.

Contents

  • grad-entry-shape.jsonl.gz — 1,602,508 rows. Post-migration price trajectories across 40,427 mints.
  • liquidity-track.jsonl — 65,861 rows. Liquidity, price, FDV and 24h flow series per position.
  • grad-early-shadow.jsonl — 38,503 rows. Exit-policy grid: one row per (position, exit configuration).
  • grad-social-shadow.jsonl — 37,401 rows. Post-migration positions with real Jupiter fills and ex-ante features.
  • exit-slippage.jsonl — 922 rows. Real exit slippage, order by order.
  • entry-exec.jsonl — 759 rows. Entry overhead: fill vs. decision price.
  • survivor-shadow.jsonl — 597 rows. Independent survivor-strategy evaluations, joinable by mint.
  • MANIFEST.json — row counts and SHA-256 per file.
  • tools/ — scripts reproducing the condition sweep and building the release.

LIMITATIONS — read before using

1. Most price series still truncate at ~36 minutes. v2 bounds this bias but does not remove it: 83.5% of mints truncate near 36 min and only 4.3% reach 190 min. Use the long subsample to correct an estimate, not to replace the population.

2. The schema changes over time. Older rows lack screenMult and exitImpactPct; newer rows lack devBuySol, migrateDelayMin and the adaptive* fields. Any loader must tolerate missing keys.

3. Single-operator data. Execution telemetry comes from one wallet's order flow. Fill quality may differ at other order sizes. Sizes and observed price impact are published so transferability can be judged.

4. posSol in exit-slippage.jsonl is mark-to-market value at exit, not entry size. It satisfies slipPct = jupOutSol/posSol − 1. Grouping returns by it measures causation backwards, because a position that fell 99% is small because it lost. Entry size lives in entry-exec.jsonl.

Privacy: the dataset contains no wallets, no keys and no transaction signatures. The release is produced by a build script that strips those fields, re-audits its own output, and fails rather than shipping a violation. Token mints and creator addresses are public on-chain data.

Not investment advice. Published for research purposes.
